details.text: Thin strokes peel off the heavy stems, like a pen easing up. It gives Kadoka a hand-drawn feel.
Extenders flare as they reach out. The k’s arm starts thin and opens to a flat, confident end.
No two ends match. The c’s top and bottom are cut at their own angles, so it never feels stamped out.
The g, j and y share one descender: a tail that sweeps left and thins out.
